subject: ob-1
title: Keyless free-tier provider plane as a first-class architecture: ~20 free cloud providers routed in-process with strategy-ordered selection, 8-hop failover, escalating cooldown ladders, self-learned rate limits from 429s, decay-weighted bandit reliability stats, and a tool-call-repair post-processor for weak free models
evidence: src/providers/free/index.ts:1-35 (contract, MAX_ATTEMPTS=8); src/providers/free/state.ts:3-6,66 (cooldowns, learned limits, bandit succ/fail pseudo-counts); src/providers/free/tool-repair.ts:280 (postProcessResponse); scripts/free-router-smoke.ts (319 LOC, CI-gated)
one_why: Every other subject treats the free tier as a promo; OB-1 makes 'works with zero account/key out of the box' the default provider plane and pays for it with real machinery (health loop, debounced persisted state, keyless endpoints, repair for the weak models that fall out of routing) - the pairing of tool-repair with bandit routing over known-weak free models is corpus-unique; concept-porting only, the 'no account' README framing itself is marketing.

subject: ob-1
title: Escalation decided by an objective signal, not a model: self-fix budget spent AND the check still red -> runTurn returns { escalate } handing the turn to Fusion best-of-N; pure shouldEscalate gate exhaustively truth-table-tested, capped at once per user turn
evidence: src/agent/loop.ts:120-128 (shouldEscalate), :796-804 (signal site); src/agent/loop.test.ts:29-33 (full 3-flag truth table); scripts/escalation-smoke.ts:1-13 (a-e decision surface via injected _callModel/verify seams)
one_why: Most quality loops either silently give up or let an LLM judge whether to keep going; OB-1's trigger is purely the verified-failure signal plus three policy flags (off by default on apply turns so escalation can't cascade), and the whole decision is testable without a model, subprocess, or fs - cleaner than deepagents' classifier ladder because no classifier participates.

subject: ob-1
title: Shipping defaults are no-prompt autopilot AND sandbox off; the on-by-default folder-trust gate downgrades only an IMPLICIT autopilot, so one /trust or any saved setting yields unapproved, unsandboxed writes and shell
evidence: src/config.ts:706 (permissionMode default 'autopilot'), :708 (sandbox default 'off'); src/index.ts:2433-2455 (trust gate scope + OB1_TRUST_GATE=0 escape); src/safety/sandbox.ts:120-125 (wrapCommand -> plain bash when mode off)
one_why: The machinery underneath is genuinely good (hardened bwrap tiers, CI-proven enforcement, loud degradation) which makes the default the whole story: trusted-folder == zero enforcement at every layer simultaneously; nanocoder-5 pattern (real jail, wrong default) mitigated but not resolved by the trust gate.

subject: ob-1
title: MockBrain scripted scenarios drive the REAL runTurn over REAL buildTools in 71 CI-gated no-key smokes, asserting wire behavior (denials, multi-tool, history shape) and invariants like 'cached system prefix stays task-agnostic'
evidence: scripts/parity-harness-smoke.ts:1-55; scripts/ci-smokes.ts:19-88 (suite = single source of truth, run on every push/PR per .github/workflows/ci.yml:36-40); escalation-/delivery-e2e-/subagents-smoke.ts all loop-level
one_why: The antipodal proof to crab-code's closed backend enum: an injectable _callModel dep plus a tmp-dir real tool registry means approval, gate, and cache invariants are property-tested end-to-end on a $0 hermetic CI tier - and escalation/delivery smokes reuse the same seam, so each new gate buys its e2e test cheaply.

subject: ob-1
title: bwrap capability probed with the EXACT runtime argv and tiered hardened->base->none so an old bwrap still sandboxes instead of silently dropping to none; CI proves enforcement live (net denied, writes confined) with a connectivity baseline that makes the denial asserts meaningful
evidence: src/safety/sandbox.ts:26-49 (argv-derived probe, tiers), :57-79 (SBPL quote/newline injection guards on embedded paths), :92-114 (--cap-drop ALL, --new-session vs TIOCSTI); scripts/bwrap-enforce.ts:25-55; .github/workflows/ci.yml:53-73 (installs bwrap, re-enables unprivileged userns)
one_why: Two failure modes other subjects miss are engineered out: subset-probes that pass while the real argv fails, and old-bwrap hosts silently losing their previously-working sandbox; the CI job even flips Ubuntu's AppArmor userns restriction so the test cannot self-skip into vacuous green.

subject: ob-1
title: Gate ordering before every mutating call: declarative deny/allow/warn rules (.ob1/policy.json, highest-priority match) -> finite consumable /allow capability tokens -> interactive approval, with forceAsk tools (public tunnel) prompting even in autopilot and an empty rule condition matching NOTHING
evidence: src/safety/policy.ts:43-45,62-70; src/agent/loop.ts:911-947 (ordering incl. forceAsk at :940-947); scripts/policy-smoke.ts + approval-tokens-smoke.ts (CI)
one_why: The empty-condition-matches-nothing rule kills the classic policy foot-gun (a typo'd condition that allows everything), and finite decrementing tokens are a sharper grant model than standing 'always allow git'; non-TTY denial is honestly reported as 'auto-denied, can't prompt' rather than a fake 'user denied' (loop.ts:948-960).

subject: ob-1
title: Two context tiers on one model-scaled budget: deterministic eviction at 60% of (window - output reserve) with path-aware protection of the freshest read of every file, LLM-summary at 85% whose cut walks past orphaned tool_results that would 400 the next call
evidence: src/agent/context.ts:42-54 (budgetChars, fractions), :96-135 (protected-latest-read eviction), :172-178 (orphan tool_result guard); src/agent/loop.ts:614-619 (thresholds track the RESOLVED model)
one_why: A 1M-window model is no longer compacted at 128k thresholds because the router's resolved model drives the arithmetic; the path-aware protection encodes the lesson that dumb age-based eviction makes the model hallucinate files it already read, and eviction invalidates the read-dedup cache so a pointer can never reference evicted content.

subject: ob-1
title: System prompt split into one cached stable block (instructions, AGENTS.md, skills, repo map) and an uncached volatile tail (per-turn semantic memory, date, model identity), with mid-stream retry hints appended as extra UNcached blocks so the warm prefix survives retries - and a CI test asserting the cached prefix stays task-agnostic
evidence: src/agent/loop.ts:270-312 (stable/volatile split), :688-695 (retry hint as uncached extra block); scripts/parity-harness-smoke.ts:41-49 (cache-boundary invariant test)
one_why: The invariant is pinned by a test rather than convention: per-turn task guidance (quality contract) is verified to land OUTSIDE the breakpoint, which is exactly the drift most subjects reintroduce when adding per-turn context.

subject: ob-1
title: The self-fix loop may not green itself by weakening tests: during a correction round a write to a test-pattern path is REFUSED, after any observed failure it is allowed but flagged loudly in the transcript and quality ledger
evidence: src/agent/loop.ts:889-907 (guard + flag sites), :826-843 (flagged edits printed on the green outcome); src/agent/test-guard.ts:12-15 (refuse|flag|off); src/agent/test-guard.test.ts (97 LOC)
one_why: Closes the one exploit every auto-verify loop has - delete the test to pass the build - with a two-strength posture (hard refuse only where the incentive is acute: mid self-fix; loud flag elsewhere so a human, not the model, decides); no other subject guards the verifier against the verified.

subject: ob-1
title: Weak-model degenerate-turn guards: whole-message prose or serialized-JSON tool calls (anchored, arg-shaped, so explanatory text mentioning tools is not flagged) and false capability refusals get one scripted nudge to re-issue REAL tool calls, then an honest 'nothing was done' outcome
one_why: A failure mode unique to cheap/weak free-tier models made first-class - the turn that 'did' work but executed nothing - with the anchoring deliberately conservative (requires kwarg syntax inside parens so 'done (first attempt)' passes); the dogfooding cases are cited inline (web_search x25, task-09).

subject: ob-1
title: 11 src modules carry a first-line 'parity with claw-code's X' header - original Apache-2.0 TypeScript, but the feature list is deliberately modeled on claw-code, which the corpus already flags as a Claude Code derivative (claw-code-1)
evidence: src/safety/policy.ts:1, src/eval/parity.ts:1, src/agent/hooks.ts:1, src/agent/approval-tokens.ts:1, src/agent/claims.ts:1, src/agent/green-contract.ts:1, src/agent/recovery.ts:1, src/config-validate.ts:1, src/context/git-state.ts:1, src/context/lsp.ts:1, src/safety/bash-validation.ts:1
one_why: Not a code fork (no shared code lineage, census 'original' holds), so calibration rule (a) does not bind, but lineage stats should trace concept genealogy claude-code -> claw-code -> ob-1 for approval tokens, policy/trust, hooks, recovery recipes and the mock parity harness itself; unusually honest for a lineage this indirect.

subject: ob-1
title: A real eval product exists (typed task suite, solo/fusion/council/personas modes, report template) but eval.yml is workflow_dispatch + secrets-only, so no model behavior is ever gated on push/PR
evidence: .github/workflows/eval.yml:3-13 (dispatch-only inputs), :23-28 (secrets), :47-51 (self-skips without creds); eval/tasks/*.json (typed tasks); docs/evals.md
one_why: Per the frozen errata the 8-rung verification ceiling needs evals-in-CI; ob-1 is one secrets-policy away from being the corpus's first eval-gated repo - the deterministic hermetic tier is already exemplary, so this is the last missing rung (understanding: free-model evals are nondeterministic, which is likely why it stayed manual).

subject: ob-1
title: TUI tested under a REAL pseudo-terminal in CI with a pyte terminal emulator asserting render persistence and streaming hygiene (no overflow garbage, pinned input), separate from the in-memory ink-testing-library smoke
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:27-49 (pip install pyte; tui-pty.py; stream-pty.py); scripts/tui-pty.py (297 LOC), scripts/stream-pty.py (143 LOC)
one_why: Catches the class of bugs component tests structurally cannot - line-overflow garble, scrollback commit errors, input repaint during streaming - by emulating the actual screen rather than the React tree; pairs with slash-menu-smoke's meta-test that every /help command is reachable in the TUI.

subject: ob-1
title: Project memory as a sqlite graph with depth-capped grounded reflection: a LLM-managed evolution pass (ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP with id-validation) plus synthesis of 'reflection' facts at level max(source)+1 that cannot recurse into reflection-of-reflection beyond the cap
evidence: src/memory/store.ts:19-43 (brain seam, reflection_level semantics), :80 (schema); src/memory/reflect.ts (shouldReflect, MAX_REFLECTION_DEPTH); scripts/memory-reflect-smoke.ts + memory-evolve-smoke.ts + memory-rank-smoke.ts (recency/importance/relevance re-rank, CI)
one_why: Most subjects stop at store-and-search or flat scratchpad memory; OB-1 consolidates and distills with bounded abstraction depth and invalidates edges in the exported DOT/HTML graph - the depth cap is the guard against confabulation spirals that unbounded reflection invites.

subject: ob-1
title: Identical-call breaker scoped to NON-mutating tools (exact name+input signature, default 3 strikes, model told the result won't change) with mutations exempt because the diff preview already gives feedback, plus a 1000-step runaway backstop that stops with work kept and a resumable message instead of killing the turn
one_why: Smaller than 3code's fingerprint window or dvalincode's triple detector, but the mutating-exempt asymmetry is a thought-through distinction none of them make (a re-applied edit is rare and already visible), and the stop message treats a tripped cap as pause-not-failure ('say continue') rather than an error.

subject: ob-1
title: /rewind on a SHADOW git repo (own GIT_DIR under the data dir, project as work-tree): snapshots the real filesystem state before every prompt so run_bash-made changes (rm/mv/sed) are revertible too, never touching the user's .git, and works in non-git directories - ON by default
evidence: src/agent/checkpoint.ts:1-21 (design + why); src/config.ts:709 (checkpoint default true); scripts/rewind-smoke.ts (real-repo isolation, CI)
one_why: Tool-only file histories (Claude Code's checkpoints) cannot undo shell damage; the shadow-repo shape gets whole-worktree revert without polluting the user's repo, and allow-empty commits mean every prompt yields a restore point even when the diff is empty.
